newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm on good foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm on good foreign demand.

text.p: Irish government bonds firmed in busy late trade on Friday on good foreign demand as the market anticipated a successful Ecofin meeting in Dublin, dealers said.
The meeting of European Union finance ministers takes place on Saturday and among the main EMU issues under discussion is a currency stability pact.
"Irish bonds are very well bid as the tone set from the start of the week has continued. We have out-performed both German bunds and UK gilts," one dealer said.
"The market expects this weekend's Ecofin meeting to be a success and this has helped sentiment too," the dealer added.

By 1510 GMT, the 8.00 percent bond due 2000 had gained 22p from Thursday's close to 104.88 to yield 6.48 percent while the 8.00 percent bond due 2006 had risen 55p from the close to 105.70 to yield 7.05 percent.
Dealers said a close eye is likely to be kept on the U.S. ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on September 24 amid talk of a possible rise in interest rates.
Treasuries remained stuck in narrow ranges, little changed in a data-sparse session. Analysts said U.S. dealers seemed to be taking positions ahead of the FOMC.
"The consensus seems to be that we will see a 25 basis points rise in U.S. interest rates," the dealer said.
